_meta.indication: BAVENCIO is a PD-L1 blocking antibody indicated for the treatment of adults and pediatric patients 12 years and older with metastatic Merkel cell carcinoma (MCC).

pivotal_trials.design: Single-arm, open-label, multicenter study; patients received avelumab 10 mg/kg IV every two weeks until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity.
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with metastatic Merkel cell carcinoma who had progressed following at least one prior systemic chemotherapy regimen.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Confirmed best overall response rate (ORR) by RECIST 1.1 per independent review committee, with duration of response (DOR) as the key secondary endpoint.
pivotal_trials.result: Confirmed centrally reviewed ORR 33% (95% CI: 23, 44), including 11% CR and 22% PR; among 29 responders, DOR not reached (range 2.8 to 23.3+ months), 86% (25/29) with DOR ≥ 6 months and 45% (13/29) with DOR ≥ 12 months.

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥20%) in the JAVELIN Merkel 200 trial (N=88): fatigue (50%), musculoskeletal pain (32%), diarrhea (23%), nausea (22%), infusion-related reaction (22%), rash (22%), decreased appetite (20%), peripheral edema (20%). Serious risks include immune-mediated adverse reactions (pneumonitis, hepatitis, colitis, endocrinopathies, nephritis) and infusion-related reactions.
target_moa: Avelumab is directed against PD-L1; it inhibits the interaction between PD-L1 and its receptors PD-1 and B7-1, and can also mediate antibody-dependent cell-mediated cytotoxicity (ADCC).

rems.type: FDA determined there was no need for a REMS associated with the application.

advisory_committee.vote: The Division did not obtain the advice of the Oncologic Drug Advisory Committee (ODAC) for this BLA.

description.text: Converted dosing from weight-based 10 mg/kg every two weeks to a flat dose of 800 mg every two weeks

citations.quote: This Prior Approval Supplemental Biologics Application provides for updates to the U.S. Prescribing Information (USPI) to the Dosage and Administration, Recommended Dosage subsection (2.2) to convert from a weight-based dose regimen of 10 mg/kg every two weeks to a flat dose regimen of 800 mg every two weeks; and to the Clinical Pharmacology section to add a new Pharmacodynamics (12.2) subsection and to revise the Pharmacokinetics (12.3) subsection to support this new dosage regimen.

description.text: Added new indication for avelumab in combination with axitinib for first-line treatment of advanced renal cell carcinoma (RCC)

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental biologics application provides for a new indication for Bavencio® (avelumab) in combination with Inlyta® (axitinib) for first-line treatment of patients with advanced renal cell carcinoma (RCC).

description.text: Added new indication for maintenance treatment of locally advanced or metastatic urothelial carcinoma not progressed after first-line platinum-containing chemotherapy

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental biologics application provides for a new indication for the maintenance treatment of patients with locally advanced or metastatic urothelial carcinoma (UC) that has not progressed with first-line platinum-containing chemotherapy.

description.text: Labeling update adding overall survival results for both populations (all randomized patients and PD-L1 positive tumors) from JAVELIN Bladder 100 for maintenance treatment of advanced/metastatic urothelial cancer

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental biologics license application provides for labeling revisions to the U.S. Prescribing Information for Bavencio to add the overall survival results for both populations (all randomized patients and patients with PD-L1 positive tumors) from clinical trial JAVELIN Bladder 100.

description.text: Converted accelerated approval to regular approval for metastatic Merkel cell carcinoma in adults and pediatric patients 12 years and older

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental biologics license application provides for regular approval of BAVENCIO (avelumab) for the treatment of adults and pediatric patients 12 years and older with metastatic Merkel cell carcinoma (mMCC), in fulfillment of PMR 3185-1. This sBLA also proposes to remove the following statement from the currently approved indication: "This indication is approved under accelerated approval based on tumor response rate and duration of response. Continued approval for this indication may be contingent upon verification and description of clinical benefit in confirmatory trials. (1.1, 14.1)."

description.text: Updated labeling with final overall survival analysis from JAVELIN Renal 101 for avelumab in combination with axitinib in first-line advanced renal cell carcinoma

citations.quote: This Prior Approval Supplemental biologic license application provides the final analysis of overall survival from Study B9991003 (JAVELIN Renal 101).

surrogate_endpoint.text: Durable objective response rate (ORR and DOR), a surrogate endpoint reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit (improved survival) in patients with metastatic MCC.

citations.quote: Durable objective response rate of sufficient magnitude is a surrogate endpoint that is reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit (i.e., improved survival) in patients with metastatic MCC.

confirmatory_requirement.text: Conduct and submit results of a multicenter clinical trial (PMR 3185-1) confirming clinical benefit of avelumab in patients with metastatic MCC who have not received prior systemic therapies.

citations.quote: 3185-1 Conduct and submit the results of a multicenter clinical trial confirming the clinical benefit of avelumab in patients with metastatic Merkel cell carcinoma (MCC) who have not received prior systemic therapies for metastatic MCC. The trial will enroll at least 100 patients followed for a minimum of 12 months, in order to establish the objective response rate and characterize the durability of response for first-line treatment of metastatic MCC. All patients will be followed for overall survival until at least 70% of patients have died in order to characterize effects on survival. An analysis of overall survival compared to historical control data will be provided.

basis.text: Breakthrough Therapy Designation was granted on November 17, 2015 for metastatic MCC.

citations.quote: The clinical review team considered these data to be preliminary evidence of a substantial improvement over salvage chemotherapy treatment options. On November 17, 2015, BTD was granted.

basis.text: Fast Track Designation was granted October 1, 2015 for investigation of avelumab in patients with metastatic MCC.

citations.quote: On October 1, 2015, FTD was granted for the investigation of avelumab for the treatment of patients with metastatic MCC to demonstrate a clinically important and statistically robust improvement in PFS for patients treated with avelumab compared to available therapy.

orphan_indication.text: Orphan drug designation was granted September 21, 2015 for the treatment of MCC.

citations.quote: On September 21, 2015, avelumab was granted orphan drug designation for the treatment of MCC.

basis.text: The application was reviewed under Priority review.

summary.text: Avelumab (BAVENCIO) received accelerated approval under 21 CFR 601 subpart E for metastatic Merkel cell carcinoma, based on durable objective response rate as a surrogate endpoint, with a required confirmatory trial in treatment-naive metastatic MCC. The application had orphan drug (Sept 2015), fast track (Oct 2015), and breakthrough therapy (Nov 2015) designations and was reviewed under priority review.

citations.quote: It is recommended that approval for avelumab be granted under the provisions of accelerated approval delineated in 21 CFR 601, Subpart E for the treatment of adults and pediatric patients 12 years and older with metastatic Merkel cell carcinoma (MCC). All primary scientific discipline reviewers concur in this recommendation.
Durable objective response rate of sufficient magnitude is a surrogate endpoint that is reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit (i.e., improved survival) in patients with metastatic MCC.
In 2015, Orphan Drug, Fast Track, and Breakthrough Therapy designations were granted for the treatment of MCC.
